The full arbitrary-schedule sampling question remains unresolved in this return. I have not constructed an $\eta_{\mathrm{sample}}(a,k,d,g)>0$ for the entire stated class, and I have not proved a model-preserving robust sampling-hardness obstruction.

There is a concrete generative advance: a polynomial-bit sampler, together with uniformly controlled pinned normalization, for native schedules made of sufficiently long, overlapping fixed-size patch layers. This uses the actual scheduled GKLS channels, allows nonunital perturbations and arbitrary finite local POVMs, and handles binary durations. The missing extension is to arbitrary simultaneous couplings and short-time transients.

I also obtained an explicit native failure of a proposed hardness route: continuous replacement noise destroys the usual uniform-output anticoncentration property of the cited ideal 2D quench ensemble. That result does not establish sampling easiness or hardness for the full class.
